newsitem.title: CANADA: Second St. Lawrence Seaway lane to reopen Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Second St. Lawrence Seaway lane to reopen Saturday.

text.p: The second of two ship lanes in the St. Lawrence Seaway should reopen Saturday once the Canadian Mariner is dislodged from the river bottom after it ran aground Wednesday, a Seaway spokeswoman said.

"The second lane should reopen Saturday. Barges are coming in from Valleyfield (Quebec) and should start unloading the Canadian Mariner this evening," St. Lawrence Seaway Authority spokeswoman Sylvie Moncion said in French.
No one was injured when the Canadian Mariner ran aground at Alex Bay near Brockville, Ontario, at 1030 EDT Wednesday. Barges will unload part of its 25,060 wheat cargo, she said.
"It's not delaying ships very much to go through one lane only--they're only delayed by 10 or 15 minutes," Moncion said.
The ship is owned by Upper Lakes Shipping of Toronto and was contracted by Seaway Bulk Carriers of Winnipeg, she said.
The ship was insured but the extent of damage was not yet known.
The vessel was to transfer its cargo to an ocean vessel in Quebec City, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
